document_metadata.document_title: New Jersey Stormwater Best Management Practices Manual — Chapter 5 (Quantity and Quality Standards and Computations) and Chapter 9.7 (Small-Scale Bioretention Systems)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: NJDEP Water Quality Design Storm (WQDS): 1.25 inches of rain falling nonuniformly over 2 hours (N.J.A.C. 7:8-5.5). NRCS methodology is used to compute WQDS runoff volume, peak rate, and hydrograph; BMPs such as small-scale bioretention must store/treat the entire WQDS volume.
peak_flow_calculation_method: USDA NRCS methodology (NRCS Runoff Equation and Dimensionless Unit Hydrograph; NEH Part 630 Hydrology Chapters 7, 9, 10, 15, and 16)
approved_bmp_categories: Small-scale bioretention systems (rain gardens, stormwater planters, bioswales, tree pits)

evidence.excerpt: the Stormwater Management rules at N.J.A.C. 7:8-5.7 allow only the methodology listed below... The USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) methodology, including the NRCS Runoff Equation and Dimensionless Unit Hydrograph as described in Chapters 7, 9, 10, 15 and 16, Part 630 Hydrology, National Engineering Handbook (NEH)
The key component of the NRCS runoff equation is the NRCS Curve Number (CN), which is based on soil permeability, surface cover, hydrologic condition and antecedent moisture.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Multi-chapter excerpt (Ch5 July 2023 calculations/standards + Ch9.7 Jan 2026 small-scale bioretention), not the full NJ BMP Manual. WQDS (1.25 in/2-hr) and quantity storms (2-/10-/100-year current and projected) are from Ch5; GI BMP inventory is incomplete relative to the full Chapter 9 series. N.J.A.C. 7:8-5.7 requires NRCS methodology but does not mandate a specific software package (HydroCAD appears only in worked examples). TR-55 is cited as superseded by NEH Part 630.
